method: SERV Kronos does not return its audit log over the API. Each prompt gets two Kronos calls: the exact prompt run as-is on a text-only probe case (auditedRun, with its request id and answer), and the same bytes supplied as data to a Kronos-enabled audit prompt that returns the findings. See docs/KRONOS.md.

prompts.name: underwriter
prompts.note: Exact system string sent by underwriteRequest(CASES.clean). Its guide hash must equal RATING_GUIDE_HASH in src/underwrite.ts.
prompts.summary: The prompt leaves evidence classification and some peril estimates insufficiently specified, which can change underwriting results.

findings.issue: It does not say how to identify an untrusted document when the supplied documents are not explicitly labeled. Reviewers could include or exclude the same document, changing what evidence is considered and potentially the tampered estimate.
findings.suggestion: Define untrusted documents as documents supplied by the agent or an external sender, and identify any other supplied records as records.

findings.clause: “You estimate… the probability that [the action] causes a loss under each covered peril” and “Anchors (adjust for the evidence you see)”
findings.issue: The prompt gives anchors for only some cases and no method for estimating probabilities in other evidence scenarios, including unauthorized risk. Careful reviewers could assign materially different probabilities to the same evidence.
findings.suggestion: Add a short rule for estimating probabilities when no anchor applies, including how to assess unauthorized risk.

prompts.name: claims-judge
prompts.note: Exact claims-judge system prompt. guideSha256 signs BOND_WORDING, the wording the judge applies.
prompts.summary: The prompt leaves outcome-relevant coverage, exclusion, evidence, and input-handling decisions unresolved.

findings.clause: “any action other than the bonded one (a different amount, payee or pay-to address)” and covered peril “overbilling (the excess only)”
findings.issue: A different amount can both trigger the action-mismatch exclusion and constitute covered overbilling; the prompt does not say which rule prevails or how to treat the excess versus the matching amount.
findings.suggestion: State whether overbilling is an exception to the different-amount exclusion and specify how the covered excess is calculated.

findings.clause: “covered peril: payee_not_vendor, duplicate, overbilling (the excess only), unauthorized, tampered”
findings.issue: The peril labels are not defined. Reviewers could classify the same evidence differently, changing whether the loss is covered.
findings.suggestion: Add brief definitions for each peril, including the evidence or comparison used to establish it.

findings.issue: It does not say whether any recovery bars the entire claim or whether only the unrecovered balance is excluded.
findings.suggestion: Specify that recovered amounts are deducted from the claimed loss, or state that any recovery bars the claim.

findings.clause: “claims filed more than 30 days after binding”
findings.issue: The prompt does not identify what event or date counts as filing, so the same claim could be considered timely or late.
findings.suggestion: Define filing as receipt of the claim by Bonded and specify the date source used.

findings.clause: “a claim evidenced only by the insured's own statement, with no third-party document”
findings.issue: It does not say what qualifies as a third-party document or how to treat documents whose source or reliability is disputed.
findings.suggestion: Define qualifying third-party evidence and how disputed provenance is handled.

findings.clause: “reads the whole original case, the underwriter's quote and the claim evidence together”
findings.issue: The quote may contain a probability, but the prompt does not say what that probability means or whether it affects claim adjudication; reviewers could give it different weight.
findings.suggestion: State that quote probabilities are informational only and do not determine coverage, or define their role.

findings.issue: The prompt requires verbatim transcription of hidden text without specifying how the judge receives or identifies it; the requirement may be impossible to apply consistently to supplied documents.
findings.suggestion: Limit transcription to text actually available in the provided document representations and require noting when hidden text cannot be accessed.
